error_description: Sodium to hypernatremia is sound, but hypernatremia is at most an occasional, incidental finding in CA-VA deficiency (the defining labs are ammonia, lactate, bicarbonate, glucose); a high sodium says essentially nothing about this disease.

A lupus-anticoagulant coagulation ratio (dRVVT screen/confirm) has been mapped to the near-root term 'Abnormality of immune system physiology', and a LOW ratio is actually the normal result; chaining that to a hypopigmentation syndrome that carries the same umbrella term yields a spurious association.
error_theme: test mapped to unrelated broad phenotype

error_description: An antigen-specific antibody (anti-gliadin IgA, a coeliac serology) is treated as if it measured total serum IgA; a high gliadin IgA titre does not indicate hypergammaglobulinaemia A, so the link to a congenital neutropenia with raised IgA is unfounded.
error_theme: specific antibody equated with total immunoglobulin

error_description: Hypoglycemia is a very rare (<5%) and non-characteristic feature of primary Fanconi syndrome and is carried by 200+ diseases; in addition the test is a 5-hour post-100 g glucose-load timepoint (reactive hypoglycemia testing), not a baseline glucose.

The curator text is right (alloisoleucine is expected to be absent/normal, distinguishing this from MSUD), but the edge labels a normal analyte as a 'biomarker' with result 'other'; a consumer of the triple would infer alloisoleucine is abnormal in this disease when it is really a pertinent negative.

Erythropoietin concentration is a hormone level, not a measure of red cell morphology; mapping both high and low EPO to 'Abnormal erythrocyte morphology' is wrong, and that phenotype is itself very rare in autoerythrocyte sensitization (a psychogenic purpura), so the association is spurious.
error_theme: test mapped to unrelated broad phenotype

error_description: Raised ACTH is a genuine feature of POR-deficiency CAH, but this code is an ACTH value 1 h after a glucagon stimulation, where a rise is the expected physiological response and 'high' is not interpretable as baseline ACTH excess.

Hypoglycemia is not a recognised hallmark of familial hypertrophic cardiomyopathy 27; the 'obligate (100%)' frequency looks like an artefact of a small case series, and the test is a 7.5 h timepoint after an unspecified challenge rather than a plain glucose.

Elevated LH (hypergonadotropic state) is a true feature of premature ovarian failure 8, but the test is a 2 h post triple-bolus (combined pituitary stimulation) timepoint, where LH is expected to rise in normal people; 'high' here needs stimulated-response criteria, not baseline ones.

Hypoglycemia is a very rare (<5%), nonspecific feature of histiocytoid cardiomyopathy, and the test is a 4 h post-glucose-load timepoint rather than a fasting/random glucose, so the association has negligible value.
Elevated LH is a real feature of ovarian dysgenesis, but the test is the 7th specimen of an unspecified stimulation series; a stimulated LH value cannot be read as baseline 'elevated circulating LH'.

Urine sediment RBC count to hematuria is sound, but hematuria is a very rare (<5%), nonspecific finding in Castleman disease and occurs in 140+ diseases; the test has no discriminating value for this disease.

A LOW erythrocyte heptacarboxylporphyrin has no pathological meaning (only elevation matters, and the normal amount is near zero), yet it is mapped to a generic 'abnormal' term; the term also says 'circulating' while the specimen is red cells.

Raised ACTH is the defining lab feature of familial glucocorticoid deficiency, but this code is a 2 h post-challenge timepoint of an unspecified stimulation test, so 'high' is not equivalent to elevated baseline ACTH.

A complement-fixation titre against a single virus (echovirus 9) is treated as a measure of total immunoglobulin; a low/absent titre is the normal result in anyone not recently infected and does not indicate hypogammaglobulinaemia, so the link to agammaglobulinaemia is not supported by this test.
error_theme: specific antibody equated with total immunoglobulin

error_description: A single-ear, single-frequency (right ear, 1000 Hz) threshold only characterises the hearing-loss phenotype; it cannot diagnose a specific genetic subtype (DFNB104 needs molecular testing), and one frequency in one ear is far narrower than the 'audiologic characterization' the record describes.

Low LH is obligate in hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and a blunted stimulated response is clinically relevant, but the test is the 7th specimen of an unspecified challenge, so 'low' means a blunted response under challenge-specific criteria rather than the baseline 'decreased circulating LH' phenotype.

The disease record lists the immunoglobulin abnormality as excluded (0%), so the chain asserts an association the source explicitly denies; independently, a low allergen-specific IgE (bovine gelatin) is the normal result and is not an abnormality of circulating immunoglobulin concentration.

Inappropriately raised C-peptide is characteristic of HNF1A hyperinsulinism, but it is defined during hypoglycemia/fasting; a C-peptide 1 h after a glucose load is physiologically high in everyone, so 'high' on this challenge timepoint does not map to the phenotype.

Hyperglycemia is annotated as explicitly NOT a feature of familial renal glucosuria (normal blood glucose with glucosuria is the definition of the disease), but the negation was dropped and the association asserted in the positive; the test is also an OGTT timepoint.

ACTH-resistant adrenal insufficiency with high ACTH is a real feature of triple-A syndrome, but the test is ACTH 1 h after a glucose dose (a dynamic-test timepoint), not a baseline ACTH, so the abnormal-result interpretation does not transfer.

The CSF abnormality is annotated as explicitly NOT a feature of hereditary spastic paraplegia 12, yet the chain asserts it positively; in addition, a low CSF lymphocyte fraction is not a meaningful abnormality and was mapped to a vague 'abnormal CSF morphology' term.

Hypoglycemia can occur in holoprosencephaly (via pituitary dysfunction) but is an uncommon, nonspecific feature shared with 200+ diseases, and the test is a 5 h post-100 g glucose-load timepoint; each step is loosely defensible but the combination carries little information.

Serum magnesium to hypomagnesemia is sound, but hypomagnesemia is a minor, case-report-level finding in dopamine beta-hydroxylase deficiency (orthostatic hypotension 1), whose characteristic labs are catecholamines; the 'frequent' label likely overstates it.

Hyperglycemia is of course central to permanent neonatal diabetes, but the test is a lactose tolerance test timepoint, where the glucose rise is read as evidence of lactase activity (and a flat curve is the abnormal result); 'high' on this test is not the hyperglycemia phenotype.

ACTH 1.5 h after IV insulin is an insulin-tolerance-test timepoint, where a rise in ACTH is the intended normal response, so 'high' is not baseline ACTH excess; ectopic ACTH secretion is also a very rare (<5%) feature of bronchial endocrine tumours.

Ionized calcium to hypercalcemia is sound and hypercalcemia/nephrocalcinosis is reported in glucose-galactose malabsorption, but it is an occasional secondary finding of a nonspecific phenotype (70+ diseases) and not useful for recognising the disease.

Pigweed IgE is a weed-pollen (aeroallergen) sensitisation; 'anti-plant product IgE' is a broad grouping term and a more specific pollen/weed-pollen IgE term would be the appropriate target if one exists in HPO (not verified here).

The code is glucose 1 minute after an IV glucose bolus (IVGTT), when glucose is at its peak; a 'low' flag at that point is relative to a challenge-specific expectation (or a sampling/infusion problem), not clinical hypoglycemia.

A normal C-peptide 1.5 h after glucose only shows a normal stimulated response at that timepoint; it cannot 'rule out' abnormal C-peptide in general (e.g. inappropriate fasting C-peptide in insulinoma/hyperinsulinism), so the exclusion is too strong for a challenge-test code.

A low allergen-specific IgE (boysenberry) is the normal, expected result in non-allergic people and does not measure total immunoglobulin; it was mapped (as 'low') to a nondirectional 'abnormal immunoglobulin concentration' term and then chained to X-linked SCID.
error_theme: specific antibody equated with total immunoglobulin

error_description: Hyperglycemia is recorded as excluded (0%) in this keratoderma syndrome, but the exclusion was ignored and a positive association generated; the test is additionally a lactose-tolerance timepoint rather than a diagnostic glucose.
